DKSAP-IoT reduces computational overhead by at least 50% compared to standard DKSAP
The protocol saves transmission of 72·(N-1) bytes for N stealth transactions
Random-point scalar multiplication on Raspberry Pi 3 takes 3.67 ms
Fixed-point scalar multiplication on Raspberry Pi 3 takes 3.12 ms
Cryptographic hash function computation takes 5.26 µs on Raspberry Pi 3
Hash function is approximately 1000 times faster than scalar multiplication
The implementation uses a 283-bit binary Koblitz curve (sect283k1)
DKSAP-IoT reduces random-point scalar multiplications from N to 1 on sender side
DKSAP-IoT reduces random-point scalar multiplications from N to 1 on receiver side
DKSAP-IoT reduces fixed-point scalar multiplications from 2N to N+1 on sender side
The protocol maintains two key pairs: scan key pair and spend key pair
Neither the scan public key nor spend public key appear on the blockchain
The shared secret is updated using the formula: h_cntB ← H(h_cntB-1)
BLAKE-256 was chosen as the hash function for high performance across platforms
The protocol provides receiver anonymity through ECDLP difficulty
Forward privacy is achieved through one-way properties of the hash function
Stealth transactions without ephemeral keys are indistinguishable from regular transactions
The first transaction between peers requires ephemeral key generation
Subsequent N transactions use pre-computed shared secrets
Sensitive information (tables and private keys) should be stored in encrypted form
The protocol was implemented in C using GNU C Compiler
libsect283k1 library uses lambda coordinates and window τNAF method for optimization
The paper demonstrates implementation on Raspberry Pi 3 Model B
DKSAP was first fully implemented in 2014 for ShadowSend
DKSAP has been realized in Monero, Samourai Wallet, and TokenPay
